answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
Give the legs a full week off running first. Walk when you feel like moving, and let the blister close. From about day 5 or 6, if the stairs feel normal and nothing sharp shows up, a short easy jog is fine, and the week after that we can rebuild to your usual easy runs.

The Thanksgiving 10K in 5 weeks is doable, but only as a steady run, not a race. Hard 10K efforts in week 3 or 4 after a marathon are where people pick up niggles, and you have nothing to prove five weeks after a PR. If you want to toe the line with your friend and enjoy it at a conversational effort, that fits inside recovery. If you want to actually race a 10K, I would rather point you at one 8 to 10 weeks out and train for it properly.

new.analysis:
## What the race told us
You held 8:30/mi through 33 km and then paid for it over the last 10K, drifting to about 9:30/mi. Quad failure, not aerobic failure: your average heart rate was 161 and only crept to 164 late. That is a strength and durability story, not a fitness one, and it is the thing we can actually train.

## Why this week is so light
A marathon takes a real bite out of the legs, immune system and sleep, and the standard window to let that settle is one to three weeks easy with no hard efforts. Your check-in flags are consistent with that: quads wrecked, stairs hard, blister on the toe, sleep down to 6.5 hours. Running on that only delays feeling good.

## What I need from you
Tell me what you want to point at next and I will build the next block around it. The Thanksgiving 10K is one option, a short break then a winter base is another, and a spring half or marathon is a third. Any of them is fine, they just lead to different weeks.

safetyCallouts.title: Normal soreness vs something more.
safetyCallouts.body: Marathon quad and calf soreness that eases day by day is expected. If a specific spot gets sharper rather than duller over the next week, or you get swelling, dark urine or a fever, see a GP or physio and hold off running.
